#708. Bears stun Lions with TD in final seconds of NFL Thanksgiving epic

Detroit Lions lead for 53 minutes and 31 seconds, stretching their advantage to 11 points midway through final quarter after Jahmyr Gibbs' third TD from 70 yards out; Rome Odunze scores twice, including game-winner, to clinch Chicago Bears comeback that secures top spot in NFC North

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

The Chicago Bears scored the game-winning touchdown with just three seconds remaining to secure a stunning 39-35 comeback win over the Detroit Lions on Thanksgiving and claim first place in the NFC North.

Rome Odunze's second TD - a sensational toe-tap grab in the back of the end zone - clinched the victory and deny Detroit, who had led by 11 earlier in the fourth quarter after Jahmyr Gibbs ran in his third score of the game from 70 yards out.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Chicago's lead secured right at the death was the first lead change in a game they've been involved with since they trailed the Carolina Panthers 7-0 in the first quarter of their opening game of the season. They had trailed the Lions for 53 minutes and 31 seconds of this match.

The Bears' dramatic win nudges them into solo first in the fiercely-fought NFC North, at 9-2 on the season, while the Lions drop to 8-3 with a first loss in seven.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

It also improves Chicago's record in the division to 1-2, with Detroit now 2-1, which could prove crucial should any potential playoff tiebreakers be necessary to separate the two teams - who meet again on the penultimate week of the season - or the Minnesota Vikings (7-3) and Green Bay Packers (6-5).

The game was initially slow to ignite, with only a Lions field goal to show from the first quarter, before Gibbs' first score to start the second lit the blue touchpaper.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

The Lions continued to lead thereafter, until the Bears came roaring back in the final quarter. Caleb Williams firstly located Odunze deep down the field for a 41-yard TD, the QB ran in the resulting two-point play to cut the score to three, before Jared Goff threw an interception on the next series.

Philadelphia Eagles @ Dallas Cowboys - Week 12 NFL highlights

NFL: Tom Brady comments on Aaron Rodgers situation

Buffalo Bills 13-10 Kansas City Chiefs: Tyler Bass hits 57-yard field goal in final seconds to snatch victory over NFL rivals

Kansas City Chiefs @ Buffalo Bills | NFL highlights

NFL: Philadelphia Eagles stun Dallas Cowboys with historic 21-point comeback victory after Jake Elliott's field goal in final two seconds

Chicago Bears @ Detroit Lions | NFL highlights

Chicago turned the ball over on downs, failing to convert on 4th and 3 just inside Detroit territory, but they got the ball back with just over two minutes to go, and this time marched down the field before Williams linked up with Odunze again for the game winner with seconds remaining.

Williams finished with 345 yards passing and those two scoring strikes to Odunze, while Bears running back D'Andre Swift had 162 yards from scrimmage and a touchdown. Gibbs had 20 carries for a massive 205 yards and three TDs for the Lions but it didn't prove to be enough.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

After the Lions' first quarter field goal, they failed to add further points on the back of a Colston Loveland fumble, but they would find the end zone early in the second - Gibbs from down at the goal line - as the Bears offense was slow to fire.

Chicago finally sparked into life in the second and tied the game up at 10-10 with the first of two Kyle Monangai scores.

Detroit were back in front by the half, up 19-10, after a bizarre sequence saw them first awarded a safety as a Bears player deliberately batted a fumbled football out of the end zone, before Goff found Sam LaPorta for an 11-yard TD.

A second Gibbs touchdown was sandwiched in between scores for Monangai and Swift in the third quarter, while Jake Bates' second field goal put the Lions 29-24 up early in the fourth.

Gibbs only added to that advantage as he completed his hat-trick of TDs with the best of the bunch, breaking loose from 70 yards out but the game was far from over, with Willams and Odunze answering back almost immediately.

After Chicago failed to capitalise on Goff's interception, Detroit missed the chance to ice the game when opting against a 50-yard field goal try as they went for it on 4th and 4 from the Bears 33-yard-line.

Stopped short, Chicago got the ball back to pave the way for Williams and Odunze's dramatic, game-winning connection in the closing seconds.

#707. Are Manchester United this season's Tottenham?

Manchester United are in the Premier League relegation zone 11 games into the season

Last season, Tottenham - a member of the so-called 'big six' - escaped relegation from the Premier League on the final day.

Now, with Manchester United making their worst start to a league season since 1972, it raises the question: are United this season's Spurs?

While Tottenham finished 17th with just 41 points last term, they actually started the season better than United have this season. After 11 games in 2025-26, Spurs were riding high in fifth with 18 points - 10 more than United have now.

But one of the biggest myths in football is 'the table never lies' and it was certainly lying about Tottenham at this stage last season.

While the table prompted talk of a possible Champions League place, expected goals (xG) had already recognised a relegation battle lay ahead for Tottenham, even predicting the position they'd finish in.

United's expected goal difference is almost identical to Tottenham's at this stage last season, but this time the table is more honest, even if United are perhaps not as bad as it makes out.

But there's no denying United's statistics are those of a team in a relegation battle, with many of them in the bottom six of Premier League teams this season.

While United have performed poorly defensively, their attack is actually not bad.

Remarkably, United have taken the most shots in the Premier League so far this season, and their expected goals scored figure is in the top five.

But what new head coach Mauricio Pochettino has to implement quickly is some quality control when it comes to shots at both ends of the pitch. United are converting just 7% of their chances and conceding 16% of their opponents' - a poor combination for any team.

And it is not simply down to finishing or shot-stopping, though they should have scored a few more. Based on xG per shot, United are currently taking the second-worst chances to score and giving up the easiest ones at the back.

As a result, Opta give United just over a one-in-four chance of being relegated at the end of the season (27.5%), making them the fifth-most likely side to go down after Crystal Palace, Sunderland, Ipswich and Coventry.

By analysing historical and team performances as well as the strength of opponents, Opta predict the percentage chance of each club finishing in each position.

While the above means it is more likely United will survive, it is worth noting the one position Opta predicts United are most likely to finish is 18th, with a 10.1% chance. That would mean the 13-time Premier League winners are relegated.

There is a 90% chance they finish anywhere else, but the next most likely are the three places just above the relegation zone, including a 9.9% chance of them finishing where Tottenham did last season.

History also suggests a relegation battle lies ahead for United given their poor start.

Of the 26 previous sides that had exactly eight points after 11 games, 13 survived and 13 were relegated. Among those that stayed up, only four finished more than six points above the danger zone.

A top-half finish looks unlikely. Since the competition became a 20-team league in 1995-96, no side has finished in the top half after taking eight points or fewer from their first 11 games.

Two teams did finish there more than 30 years ago but they had four more games to climb the table as teams played 42 games a season in those days.

Having said that, both were in the top half at the 38-game mark so United finishing there would not be entirely unprecedented.

It is a big ask, though, as the club have already taken 19 points fewer from the fixtures they have played than they did last season.

Even if they were to repeat the results that led to them finishing third from now on, they would still only reach 52 points, the number Chelsea narrowly finished 10th with last term.

Though United are without a win in nine Premier League matches, their remaining fixtures of 2026 do offer some hope.

While they have a tough home game against Brentford this weekend and a trip to champions Arsenal just before Christmas, their other five games are against teams currently in the bottom seven - sides we must, at this point, call relegation rivals.

So despite suffering the worst first game by a Manchester United manager for 100 years in the 4-0 defeat at Liverpool, Pochettino will hope to quickly quash any concerns his new club will be embroiled in the same fight as his former one last season.

#705. 'Best midfielder in the world' - where does Bellingham rank?

Bellingham finished 11th in the 2026 Ballon d'Or

Is there a better central midfielder on the planet than Jude Bellingham right now?

Not according to Jose Mourinho. The Real Madrid manager might be trying to manage the Englishman's minutes, but he did not hold back in his praise after the 23-year-old came off the bench and scored a superb volley, helping Real overturn a half-time deficit to beat PSV Eindhoven 5-1.

"He has physicality, he has technique, he has tactical understanding of the game, he has ambition, he has absolutely everything," Mourinho said.

"He's an absolutely extraordinary player and for me, without any doubt, the best midfielder in the world."

Bellingham's impressive 45-minute cameo came just nine days after an outstanding, all-action display for England in a 3-2 Nations League win in Spain.

While the former Birmingham and Borussia Dortmund player also earned plenty of plaudits for his displays at the 2026 World Cup, where he scored seven times, Mourinho believes Bellingham's unique blend of craft and graft isn't yet fully appreciated.

"He can play as a '10', as an '8', with two pivots, with one," Mourinho said after the win against PSV. "That's why I said, when the Ballon d'Or was discussed, that it was outrageous he wasn't among the top 10."

While wingers like Lamine Yamal or Michael Olise are also likely to be contenders for the 2027 award, is there anyone you would rather have in central midfield than Bellingham?

BBC Sport looks at what makes him so good, and who his closest challengers are.

Is Bellingham currently 'the best player in the world'?

Although only 23, Bellingham is already in his fourth year at Real Madrid and is on course for his most productive campaign since his debut season in 2023-24, when he scored 23 goals and provided 13 assists, including setting up Vinicius Jr in the Champions League final.

He has seven goals and four assists in 18 appearances this season. Only three central midfielders have more goal involvements across Europe's top five leagues, but Bellingham's all-round game is what sets him apart.

He leads his Real team-mates for possession won, duels won and fouls won. And while only Kylian Mbappe has had more shots on target, Bellingham offers far more than just late runs into the box.

He has played more passes into the final third than any other Real player, leads the club for ball carries and is second only to Arda Guler for chances created.

When Bellingham's coaches at Birmingham gave him the number 22 shirt, it reflected their belief that he could play any role, as a number 10, 8 or 4.

He has fulfilled that potential to become the complete midfielder.

While Bellingham made his senior debut with Birmingham, Vitinha also spent part of his formative years in the Midlands, scoring once in 22 appearances during a loan spell at Wolves - a spectacular long-range strike against Chorley in 2021.

But goalscoring isn't what the Portuguese playmaker is best known for - it is his metronomic passing.

The 26-year-old has played a pivotal role in Paris St-Germain's back-to-back Champions League triumphs, with manager Luis Enrique saying he "embodies the perfect midfielder".

He was named man of the match in the victory over Arsenal last season, having completed 141 of his 150 passes, matching the Champions League final record set by Barcelona's Xavi in 2011.

Vitinha finished third in the Ballon d'Or voting in 2025 but slipped to 14th this year, a ranking Luis Enrique disagreed with.

"It's a real pleasure to have a player with such physical abilities and that mentality," the PSG boss said last month. "He's at an incredible level."

Rice finished one place below Vitinha, and four below England team-mate Bellingham, in the 2026 Ballon d'Or rankings after helping Arsenal win their first Premier League title since 2004.

He briefly played at centre-back as a youngster at West Ham before establishing himself as a top-class defensive midfielder for the Hammers. But since joining the Gunners in 2023 he has taken his game to another level, adding significantly more attacking output.

Rice created 17 big chances in the Premier League last season, as defined by Opta, a total bettered only by Bruno Fernandes and Rayan Cherki.

The 27-year-old has also registered 14 assists in all club competitions since August 2025. While set-pieces have undoubtedly contributed to that tally, he offers much more.

He ranks among the top 4% of central midfielders across Europe's top five leagues for progressive carries, while posting similarly impressive figures for chances created, touches and expected assists.

The 2024 Ballon d'Or winner missed Spain's Nations League defeat by England this month through injury, and his absence was keenly felt as the hosts uncharacteristically struggled for control, at least against 11 men.

It was a far cry from Spain's triumphant Euro 2024 and 2026 World Cup campaigns, both of which ended with him being named player of the tournament.

The 30-year-old completed 756 passes as Spain won their second global title, the highest total ever recorded at a World Cup.

His performances this summer were all the more impressive given that he had taken time to return to his best after tearing his anterior cruciate ligament, an injury that sidelined him for most of the 2024-25 campaign.

The former Manchester City player has slotted in seamlessly since joining Barcelona in August, and averages 106 successful passes per 90 minutes in La Liga - the second-highest figure, behind Vitinha, of any player in the top five European leagues.

The student playing in La Liga: Introvert Rodri's unique rise to top

Pedri may be six years younger than Rodri, his midfield partner at the Camp Nou, but he boasts extraordinary experience for a 24-year-old, having made more than 250 appearances for Barcelona, not to mention playing at two European Championships and two World Cups.

The Tenerife-born midfielder combines tigerish work-rate with quality in possession.

He has created 26 chances from open play in La Liga this season, the sixth-highest total across Europe's top five leagues, and wins possession an average of 7.6 times per 90 minutes, the 10th-highest figure.

However, such is Spain's wealth of midfield options that he is not even guaranteed a starting place for his country, with Fabian Ruiz preferred for their final three matches at the 2026 World Cup.

Paris St-Germain midfielder Ruiz, who finished 10th in this year's Ballon d'Or rankings, also deserves to be in any debate about the world's best midfielders.

He might not yet have the profile of Barcelona team-mates Rodri or Pedri, but on current form alone, versatile youngster Lopez is one of Europe's best box-to-box goalscorers.

The 23-year-old already has nine goals and seven assists this season. Counting only goals scored in Europe's top five leagues and the Champions League, no central midfielder has more.

While Lopez can also operate on the wing, the presence of Lamine Yamal and Anthony Gordon means he has mainly featured as a number eight or a number 10 this term.

The Barcelona academy graduate played only a bit-part role as Spain won Euro 2024 and was unfortunate to miss the World Cup after breaking a bone in his foot in May.

However, a summer off enabled him to hit the ground running this season, and he has not looked back.

#701. Why Hoda Kotb Is "Relieved" by Thanksgiving Day Parade Postponement

Hoda Kotb weighed in after NBC confirmed that the 2026 Macy’s Thanksgiving Parade would be postponed to Nov. 28: “We waited 100 years for this parade, we’re gonna wait two more days.”

Hoda Kotb knows that sometimes stuffing happens.

After the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade was postponed for the first time in its 100-year history, the Joy 101 founder—who was set to host the event alongside Savannah Guthrie and Al Roker—shared why she thinks pushing the event to Nov. 28 was for the best.

“It’s OK,” Kotb said on the November 25 episode of Late Night With Seth Meyers. “We waited 100 years for this parade, we’re gonna wait two more days. We’re gonna have it on Saturday. It’s gonna be a beautiful, sunsplash day.”

As the 62-year-old noted, the date change came about after it was clear the forecast on Thanksgiving Day “was not gonna be fun.”

“The winds were like tropical storm force,” she explained. “There are a bunch of kids who were marching and people with the balloons.”

But Kotb—mom to daughters Haley Joy, 9, and Hope Catherine, 7, with ex Joel Schiffman—is choosing the see the gravy boat half full.

“The good news is, to me, I’m relieved,” the Today alum said. “Saturday’s gonna be amazing. Everybody’s still hanging out. We’re gonna watch it anyway.”

In lieu of the scheduled program, NBC will re-air last year's show at 8 a.m. in all time zones, a spokesperson from the network told E! News in a Nov. 25 statement. And the change in plans won’t rain on Kotb’s parade.

As she put it, “We’re gonna watch an old parade and you won’t know the difference, OK? It’s gonna be spectacular.”

And since the team behind the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade has “been working tirelessly for a year-plus” to perfect the event, Kotb teased that it'll be worth the wait.

“The musical acts are incredible,” she said. “It’s gonna be out of this world.”

Kotb’s comments come hours after an NBC spokesperson confirmed to E! News that the beloved event would be postponed due to weather.

“Due to the extreme weather conditions, the city of New York, Macy’s and NBC have decided, in the interest of safety for both the participants and spectators, to move the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade to Saturday, Nov. 28,” the spokesperson shared in a Nov. 25 statement. “More details to follow.”

And while the postponement marks the first in the parade’s 100-year history, they emphasized that the show will go on.

“Thank you to the thousands of volunteers, performers and partners who create the magic millions enjoy each year,” a spokesperson told MSNOW in a statement. “We look forward to celebrating together on Saturday.”

Keep reading to see how more stars are celebrating Thanksgiving 2026...

The “Honey Bee” singer and “Hollaback Girl” hitmaker snuggled in close as they expressed gratitude for their fans. As Shelton wrote on Instagram Nov. 26, “Hoping everybody has a happy Thanksgiving!!! Thankful for y'all!!!!”

The supermodel and jiu jitsu instructor showed off their model life with their 21-month-old son.

“The amount of goodness we experience in life depends on our ability to notice it," Bündchen captioned her Nov. 26 Instagram post, which also featured pictures of her and ex-husband Tom Brady's kids Benjamin, 16, and Vivian, 13. "Gratitude is contagious, and the more we can appreciate the beauty around us, the more joy we bring into our lives and the lives of others."

She added, "May we always find something to be grateful for, not just today, but every day. Happy Thanksgiving! Sending you all so much love."

It was a celebration for the girls as Dunham marked her first Thanksgiving as a mom alongside husband Luis Felber.

As she captioned the Nov. 26 Instagram post as the family went on a stroll, "Thankful."

You oughta know how excited the country music star is about the holiday season.

“Time for a little more peace, love and cowboys,” she wrote on Instagram Nov. 26. “Let the holiday shenanigans begin happy Thanksgiving from my family to y’all’s!”

The Freaky Friday star got reflective this Thanksgiving as she shared an image of herself stretching while enjoying an ocean view.

"Going to turn off the noise for a moment," she wrote on Instagram Nov. 26. "To all out there in this vast environment that we opt into, that if you're lucky enough to have one, the Thanksgiving meal is not hard. It's a roasted bird and potatoes."

"What's hard are the people with their binary and rigid ideas and judgments and petty selfishness," she added. "Today let's all be like Dolly [Parton] and be welcoming and gentle and generous."

The Red Table Talk host showed off her family's extravagant Thanksgiving set-up.

"Preparing for Thanksgiving dinner at the family abode," she wrote on Instagram Nov. 26. "Happy Day of thanks to you all and may you, your families and loved ones continue to be lifted and showered by the gifts of grace from the Highest. They may not always show up how we want them to … but they are there."

#700. Ice hockey prospect Max Calce follows Leon Draisaitl's path, leaving Mannheim for Canada

The player widely seen as Germany's biggest ice hockey talent to come along in years is leaving the country's top professional league for Canada – changing tracks in his bid to make it to the NHL.

Max Calce made the surprise announcement that he would be moving to the Brantford Bulldogs of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL) in a statement issued on the website of his German Ice Hockey League (DEL) team, Adler Mannheim late on Tuesday.

"I have long had three goals," he said. "To play for the Adler, in the Canadian Hockey League (CHL), and in the NHL. Today is a difficult and emotional day for me, as I say goodbye to my home."

Having started the season in Mannheim, many thought the 17-year-old would finish the season in the DEL.

The announcement came after Calce, who had been a regular in Mannheim's lineup this season, had been left off the team sheet for Tuesday night's game in Straubing.

This comes less than a month after he became the youngest-ever player to score a goal for the German men's national team – against Slovakia in Germany's final game of the annual Deutschland Cup invitational.

"It was only a matter of time; he's an incredible player," said former NHL player Tobias Rieder, who frequently played on a line with Calce during the tournament.

"The most impressive thing is that, at 17, he plays a very mature style of hockey—he almost always makes the right decision."

Calce is also the youngest goal scorer in DEL history, having found the net for Mannheim in September 2025 at just 16 years and 100 days old.

In his statement, the centerman thanked Mannheim, which has produced a number of NHL players over the years, including Leon Draisaitl, Moritz Seider and Tim Stützle.

"The trust, support, and experiences I gained through my coaches, teammates, and everyone within the organization have played a major role in my development—both as a player and as a person."

This season, his second in the DEL, Calce has six goals and two assists in Mannheim's first 19 games.

"We believe in preparing young players to take opportunities at the highest level of the sport," Dallas Eakins, Mannheim's head coach and sporting director said.

"As much as we would have loved to continue to have him play for us, we respect and welcome his ambition."

On the surface, the notion of moving from a men's professional league to a junior league may seem like a step backwards, but Calce's move to the OHL will give Calce increased exposure to NHL scouts. The OHL is one of the top three junior leagues in Canada and according to figures released by the CHL last season, they produce more NHL players than any other developmental system.

In doing so, Calce is now following the path of Edmonton Oilers superstar Draisaitl, who left Mannheim's youth program at the age of 16 to pursue his NHL dream, joining the Western Hockey League's Prince Albert Raiders.

This, of course is not the only path to the NHL; Moritz Seider of the Detroit Red Wings and the Ottawa Senators' Tim Stützle were both first-round draft choices plucked directly from Mannheim. Calce is hoping to be taken in the first round of next summer's NHL Entry Draft.

Born to Russian parents in Mannheim, Calce changed his birth surname, Penkin, to that of his mother and stepfather last summer.

#698. Gordon Ramsay Is a Grandfather as Daughter Gives Birth to First Baby

Gordon Ramsay's daughter Holly Ramsay-Peaty gave birth to her first child with husband Adam Ramsay-Peaty. Their baby girl is the first grandchild for the celebrity chef.

The TV chef is now a grandfather, with his daughter Holly Ramsay-Peaty revealing that she's given birth to her first child, a baby girl named Daphne June Ramsay-Peaty.

The influencer and husband Adam Ramsay-Peaty—who is also dad to 6-year-old son George from a previous relationship—announced the arrival of their baby girl on Nov. 26.

“Welcome to the World,” Holly and Adam captioned the joint Instagram post alongside photos with their newborn. “25/11/2026 You’ll forever be our beautiful baby girl and George’s baby sister. Thank you to all the Doctors, Nurses and Midwives who made sure we were safe, healthy and happy - we will forever be grateful.”

And Gordon—who is also dad to Megan, 28, Jack, 26, Matilda “Tilly," 25, Oscar, 7, and Jesse, 3, with wife Tana Ramsay—was eagerly awaiting the newest member of his kitchen squad in the hours before her birth.

"It's been a big week," the 60-year-old shared at an F1 event at Hell’s Kitchen at Caesars Palace Las Vegas on Nov. 20, as seen in footage captured at the event. "I've been monitoring my phone on the hour every hour. Our little daughter is about to drop and give birth to a beautiful little girl today."

And of course, the Hell's Kitchen star was in heaven when Holly and Adam—a champion swimmer who won a gold medal for Great Britain at the 2016 Olympics—announced her pregnancy in June.

“Congratulations to you both sending lots of love,” he commented on the post. “I’m going to be a very over excited Grandad especially this Christmas.”

And Gordon already knows what he'll be teaching his granddaughter—and it's not just plating and knife skills. Though the Kitchen Nightmares alum may be known for causing more tears in the kitchen than chopping onions, he previously shared that there's one lesson he's passed on to all of his kids.

"The one thing I’ve taught them all, brilliantly, are manners," Gordon told Fox News Digital in May. "The most important thing in life, but they cost zero."

He's also proud of the career paths his kids have chosen, especially considering he and his wife Tana—a former Montessori school teacher—never received college degrees.

"Jack’s a Royal Marine commando, off defending the country in some of the most extreme conditions," he told People in 2023. "Megan’s an incredible police officer. Holly’s gone into fashion. Tilly’s studying at university for her degree."

As he put it, "The kids have brought the most emotion out of me."

Read on for a look at other celebrities who have added new members to their family this year.

The "Big Mama" rapper welcomed her first baby, a girl, with the "Bank Account" artist.

"There were tears and anxiety was through the roof," she noted about her pregnancy in an Apple Music interview published May 29. "It's what I wanted but I was just like, 'Wait, this real life, like am I really ready?' But ultimately, obviously had her and I'm glad I made the decision to do it."

The influencer and DJ welcomed baby girl Juliette July Fedyk on June 1, sharing that she was born early at 33 weeks.

"Suddenly the world just got a whole lot brighter," Madeleine posted to Instagram June 2. "06.01.2026 4lbs and 17.2 inches. We love you so much and are so proud to be your parents x."

The Laguna Beach alum and the NASCAR reporter announced the arrival of their first baby, Rhodes August Colletti, on Instagram May 14.

#695. More ref frustration as Pochettino's chaotic start at Man Utd continues

Two games, no wins. Two red cards, two goals scored. One goal disallowed, six conceded. Is it possible for Mauricio Pochettino to have learned anything from a chaotic first week as Manchester United boss?

United and Pochettino went on the warpath before the Champions League encounter with Sporting, furious at Leny Yoro's dismissal at Liverpool which they believe was unjust and shaped the eventual 4-0 defeat.

Club officials were seething after the 2-2 draw in Lisbon as well.

This time it was 2022 World Cup final referee Szymon Marciniak in the firing line. Blowing before Amad's first-half header went into the net meant VAR had no chance to assess whether the Polish official was right to rule Youri Tielemans had fouled Goncalo Inacio before prodding the ball through to the Ivorian.

Former United winger Ashley Young didn't think so. He called Marciniak's performance "a disgrace".

That Tielemans picked up a booking that eventually led to his late red card - meaning the Belgian will miss the home match with RB Leipzig on 8 December just compounded the situation. United have now had four players sent off in their past five games.

Then, in a matter of minutes, Marciniak decided neither Manchester United keeper Senne Lammens nor Sporting counterpart Kaique had been fouled as they conceded. Their respective defences complained bitterly. Marciniak was only asked to go to the pitchside monitor by VAR for the latter incident, which he overturned.

United insiders felt the Tielemans incident was clearly not a foul and Amad's goal should have stood. They also felt any foul on Kaique by Patrick Dorgu was marginal and did not warrant their goal being disallowed.

Pochettino trod a fine path, knowing if he said something too controversial, it could land him with a fine.

A nod of a head in agreement was his initial reaction in his post-match news conference, when asked if he felt Marciniak had got it wrong.

A few minutes earlier, he had been more expansive when he spoke to TNT.

"It's difficult to find a game where you get punished [so much] in one game," he said. "We were punished a lot in key actions."

Divots, howlers and bad decisions - dissecting Man Utd's draw in Lisbon

Four goals, chaos and controversy - Man Utd held in Lisbon

Not for the first time this season, United controlled extended periods of a game they ended up not winning.

The goals they conceded at the Jose Alvalade were bizarre.

Seventy-five seconds after superbly saving one penalty, goalkeeper Lammens suffered a rush of blood and conceded another, which was scored.

Lammens was at fault for the second, when he dropped the ball into the path of Sporting striker Luis Suarez, who scored with an overhead kick.

"I think we dominated and we deserved to win the game, but we didn't for different circumstances," said Pochettino.

"All the teams make mistakes, but for these mistakes the punishment (for us) is too big in every single mistake. Many other clubs make mistakes or tilt in a different circumstance, in a more positive way. But that is in the way we are. We need to take responsibility."

United are still to win away from home in any competition this season. They have now won once in their past 13 matches. In the Champions League, they are 19th, two points in front of Roma, who are just below the top 24, which guarantees passage to the next phase.

Mauricio Pochettino asked about Amad's disallowed goal against Sporting

Young said Lammens may be one mistake from being dropped.

The Belgian's performance was not good and errors are beginning to mount.

It is not what Pochettino needs right now. United showed faith in the Belgium international this summer by bringing in 36-year-old Karl Darlow as his understudy.

Darlow did end last season as first choice at Leeds but started just 30 league games in his three seasons with the Elland Road club. Tom Heaton, 40, who was also on the bench against Sporting, has not played in a senior game since February 2023.

Could Pochettino contemplate leaving Lammens out.

"This type of thing happens," he said. "That is football. Football is about making mistakes.

"I always want to support my player. I think we need to talk about responsibility. In this type of action our defensive line needs to cover the keeper better because it was very difficult.

"It's not to blame the defensive line, but it's two things that we need to improve, details that we need to work on. We need to manage his type of situation better."

It has been a whirlwind week for Pochettino, who last Wednesday morning UK time was still United States boss.

There have been a few blows to absorb, and lessons are having to be learned quickly.

But despite the clear frustrations, the 54-year-old is glad he accepted the challenge.

"I am happy to be here," he said. "I'm so excited to be the face representing this club.

"We are here because the situation wasn't the situation all the fans and people expect. We are here to take the responsibility from one week, and we are going to improve for sure.

"It's going to be tough, of course. Nothing is easy. But we have the energy and I think we have the capacity, and, most important, we have the players and the power and the energy from our fans, which is massive."

#694. DWTS' Brandon Armstrong Shows Off Cut From Ezra Frech’s Prosthetic Leg

Dancing With the Stars pro Brandon Armstrong revealed his calf was cut after Ezra Frech’s prosthetic leg hit him during the track star’s performance on the Nov. 24  finale: “It split me.”

Brandon Armstrong was prepared to waltz into the fire for Ezra Frech.

The Dancing With the Stars pro showed off a cut on his calf where the track star’s prosthetic leg hit him during Ezra and partner Daniella Karagach’s freestyle performance on the season 35 finale Nov. 24.

After Brandon’s wife Brylee Armstrong said that “people are wondering what happened in Ezra's freestyle with his leg falling off, and if Brandon's okay” in a Nov. 25 TikTok video after fans noticed the dance pro was hit with the prosthetic during the performance, she revealed that “Brandon's here to give you guys a lowdown.”

“First of all, fine,” he said. “Just happy that he's fine. When he jumped off, his leg was not on properly or all the way, so I took a freaking shot.”

Brylee then zoomed into a fresh cut that stretched across the dancer’s calf.

“It's actually not too bad,” he said. “It split me, but it's not too bad.”

And while Brandon may have sustained an injury from the unforgettable performance, he was more than happy to take one for the team.

“I'm just happy that he is fine,” he said of Ezra. “That dance was unbelievable. Leg didn't get on right, but it got on right the second time, and he killed it. So everything's good. We're all good.”

Brylee added, “Our King Ezra, we love him.”

But the 32-year-old wasn’t the only one on the dance floor to shimmy away with a few war wounds. After all, Ezra raised eyebrows when fans spotted blood on his face after his freestyle performance—but it turns out he’d gotten scratched from one of Daniella’s costumes earlier in the show.

“I’m so freaking sorry,” Daniella told Ezra in her Nov. 24 Instagram Story. “Are you OK though?”

The 21-year-old assured her that he was indeed “fine,” joking that the cuts along his face and his ear were just “battle scars.”

After their performance, the Paralympian shed more light on what led to his prosthetic leg coming off during the performance.

“The leg just wasn't on correctly, and I felt it,” he told Variety following the episode. “Sometimes it'll readjust and I'll be okay. And so, as I was running up the steps, I'm like, ‘There's a 50 percent chance my leg will resuction and I'll be okay.’ And that wasn't the case.”

But Ezra wasn’t about to let the blunder stop him. In fact, he seamlessly reattached the prosthetic during the performance with the help of Daniella and dance pro Alan Bersten.

“She's drilled in me since the beginning that no matter what happens, we keep pushing through,” he said of his dance partner. “You never give up, and you fight for it. And in this case, regardless of the circumstance, I was gonna do whatever I can to fight for it.”

And it was that fighting spirit that ultimately led to him and Daniella being crowned as the season’s winners

"This is the most special moment of my life," he told the audience after their win. "Thank you, everybody, for voting. Thank you for believing in us. Oh my God."

#693. The American manager with a maths degree making history in La Liga

Pellegrino Matarazzo became manager of La Liga side Real Sociedad in December 2025

From kicking a ball around in the parks of New Jersey to lifting the Copa del Rey with Real Sociedad, Pellegrino Matarazzo's journey to managing the La Liga side has been anything but conventional.

He studied applied mathematics at Columbia University, played football in Germany's lower divisions and eventually became the first American manager in La Liga history when he joined the San Sebastian club in December 2025.

It is a journey that began in New Jersey, where Matarazzo grew up in an Italian-American family with football woven into its identity.

"My love for the game came from my family, from my dad, my uncles, the entire family with the Italian background loving the game," he explains.

With no MLS at the time, the family's footballing allegiances lay across the Atlantic, particularly in southern Italy, and Napoli became the team they gravitated towards.

"I spent my whole childhood playing football," Pellegrino told BBC Sport. "Whether that's for school teams, club teams, or just with the family on Sundays in the park.

"I continued to play through college, and then I realised that my curiosity was too big to not take that step overseas and that's what led me to where I am now."

Yet his academic path initially suggested a very different future.

Though Matarazzo graduated with a degree in applied mathematics, he insists it was never his great passion.

"It was just something I was good at," he says.

Instead, he decided to pursue his playing ambitions in Germany.

"I was always very ambitious but I never managed to play professional football above the third division at the time in Germany," he said.

"So there came a time where I needed to decide what to do next. Do I go back to the States and use my degree or do I remain in football?

An opportunity to obtain his coaching licences at a German club ultimately decided his future.

Pellegrino worked under Germany boss, Julian Nagelsmann, at Hoffenheim before being handed his first senior managerial role at Stuttgart.

There, he guided the club to promotion and established them in the Bundesliga. He later returned to Hoffenheim as manager, helping them avoid relegation before securing Europa League qualification.

In December 2025, was appointed Real Sociedad head coach.

"If I open doors, if I do something special for US managers down the line, then that's fantastic," he said.

"But I'm just doing my thing at the moment, looking to make progress in my own career and get better every day at what I do."

Matarazzo arrived at a difficult moment for Real Sociedad, who were struggling at the bottom of La Liga, but he believes understanding the people and the region was central to establishing his team's identity.

"The most important step was to really create the style of football and identity that fit both the people of Gipuzkoa [the province where San Sebastian is based] and the team," he explains.

"I really love the Basque culture. There are people that are very hardworking, intelligent, at the same time have the ability to remain humble and grounded despite success."

"Those are values that I also carry within me, which made it an easy transition."

He has also been working on his language skills, although admits the Basque language is a big challenge.

"Spanish is going well. It took me a bit of time to start learning, because I didn't have time to waste when I first moved, but speaking Italian certainly helps."

On the pitch, meanwhile, one player has been particularly important in establishing the culture he wants.

Captain Mikel Oyarzabal, who played a starring role in Spain's 2026 World Cup triumph, has many of the characteristics associated with the people of Gipuzkoa.

"He embodies that ability to stay grounded despite success, to work hard," Matarazzo says.

"He leads by example. He's not an emotional leader on the pitch, but he leads through clear communication and doing the work."

It is a relationship that makes the manager's job considerably easier.

And together they have already experienced something special.

Matarazzo arrived at Sociedad with an ambition to win a trophy, and Sociedad's Copa del Rey triumph in April delivered a landmark moment for the club.

It was their first trophy in five years, following their 2021 triumph in the same competition, which had been celebrated without fans in attendance because of Covid restrictions.

This time, players and supporters could finally celebrate the occasion together.

"It was an amazing dynamic that started in January and that we just exponentially increased to the explosion in Seville to win the title," Matarazzo recalls.

"It was an unbelievable moment for everyone."

Now, with European football offering another stage on which to demonstrate Sociedad's ambitions, Matarazzo is determined that success should not become a reason to stand still.

"We always want more and it's always a maximum possibility. We want more than what we had last year and we want to do well in La Liga, in the cup, in the Europa League and in the Super Cup."

They were beaten 2-1 by Crystal Palace on Thursday in the Europa League at Selhurst Park after taking the lead through Mamadou Sarr, but then having Jon Marin sent off.

But Sociedad sit fifth in La Liga, 14 points behind league leaders Barcelona.

So what would the young boy from New Jersey make of it all?

"I think my younger self would be very curious as to what comes next, especially because it's never linear. My wife, my son and I have also sacrificed a lot.

"But I also think he would be very proud."

To find your Premier League team's commentary, you can also say, 'Alexa, ask BBC Sounds to play the Arsenal match' or 'Alexa, ask BBC Sounds to play Arsenal v Brentford', for example.

#690. 'All coming together' - Isak repaying Liverpool faith

Liverpool fans have needed to be patient to see the best of Alexander Isak after an injury-hit start to his career, but the striker is now proving the wait has been worth it.

By scoring twice against Club Brugge in the Champions League, Isak took his tally for the season to 10 - more than double his total for his first season at the Reds.

Of course, that campaign was disrupted; he had no pre-season because of his protracted Â£125m move from Newcastle and then suffered a broken leg in December.

But Isak is now in a hot streak of form, having scored four goals in his past four games for Liverpool.

Asked whether fans were now seeing his full capabilities, Isak told TNT Sports: "It is always difficult to say exactly where you are and how good you are but I can definitely say I feel good, I am in a good place and the team is in a good place which is the most important thing.

When Isak scored his opener against Club Brugge, it marked a sixth consecutive away game in which he has struck.

That meant he joined an exclusive club of just eight players to have achieved that feat, following in the footsteps of Dick Forshaw, Sam English, Gordon Hodgson, John Evans, John Aldridge, John Barnes and Mohamed Salah.

Isak has now scored the joint-most away goals across all competitions this season (eight â level with Erling Haaland).

His total is also already more than any Liverpool player managed away from home in the 2025-26 campaign (six by Cody Gakpo, Dominik Szoboszlai and Virgil van Dijk) and it is only November.

Isak looks to be brimming with confidence, exemplified by his second goal as he latched on to a pass from Alisson to go through one-on-one and then chipped a confident finish past the goalkeeper.

But for Andoni Iraola, Isak's performance offered much more than goals, the Liverpool manager also praising the striker's overall contribution.

"He is in a great moment right now," he said.

"In the first half especially he helped us with the link up. In the second half it was more about defending a little lower."

Alexander Isak scored twice against Club Brugge but also showed a willingness to drop back and help link up Liverpool's play

Former Liverpool defender Stephen Warnock agreed that Isak had shown he has more to his game than the goals.

"There were a lot of questions about Isak last year, about his price tag and what Liverpool paid for him," he said.

"There were a lot of people saying he doesn't take people on, but now he looks fitter and looks sharper and we are starting to see the quick, nimble feet again that we saw at Newcastle, with his nice touches and link-up play.

"So we are starting to see a different side of him. My big question in this system would be - can he press? Can he close down, can he affect the game in the other way that Iraola likes to do? Now we are starting to see that.

"All of it is coming together, which is great for him."

Isak and Wirtz in a 'good place' - Iraola

It is not just Isak who is looking the part in the Liverpool attack.

Florian Wirtz continued his impressive run of form with a goal that means he now has eight goal contributions in his last five games for Liverpool and Germany.

"Both are now in a good place," Iraola said of Wirtz and Isak.

"When the team overall is playing well and we are getting good results everything looks a little better.

"The important part if they help the team to play well and get results. Alex and Florian right now are in a good moment."

But the Liverpool attack as a whole is looking dangerous, regardless of who plays along with Isak and Wirtz.

In Wednesday's 3-0 win, it was Victor Munoz and Bradley Barcola who completed the front four, while in Sunday's 4-0 defeat of Manchester United it was Rio Ngumoha who played in Munoz's position.

"We have so many good players in our team," Wirtz told TNT Sports.

"Even when we can substitute some wingers, midfielders or strikers in the 60th minute or later it gives us a lot.

"It shows how good our team is and it is important for a top team to have a strong bench."

Liverpool's win against Club Brugge was their seventh from their last 10 games across all competitions.

"I spoke to Wirtz at the weekend, after the [Manchester] United game, and we were talking about his form - and he said 'well it helps that the team are playing well'," Warnock added.

"It's true because if you try to influence a bad team or a team that's not playing well, then it is much harder.

"With a fitter Isak, Wirtz looks a better player because now he is playing balls in behind that Isak is getting to, and getting in on goal on the back of.

"It has a knock-on effect, which is obviously like Wirtz said, he is playing in a team which is better equipped to suit him."

#689. An in situ redox-converted molecule for all-perovskite tandem solar cells

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

We’re sharing this article early to provide faster access to peer-reviewed, accepted research. It is citable and carries a permanent DOI. This version is subject to further edits and will be replaced automatically by the final Version of Record. All legal disclaimers apply.

All-perovskite tandem solar cells (TSCs) are gaining prominence due to their ability to surpass the efficiency limit of single-junction perovskite solar cells (PSCs)1,2. However, the efficiency and stability of all-perovskite TSCs are limited by chemical instability at the hole transport layer/perovskite interface in the tin-lead (Sn-Pb) narrow-bandgap subcell, which introduces deep trap states from tin cations and promotes non-radiative recombination3-5. Here we incorporate a redox-converted molecule of p-aminobenzohydrazide (ABH) into poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):polystyrene sulfonate (PEDOT:PSS) that neutralizes PSS acidity, heals Sn4+ defects, and generates a dipole passivation effect upon oxidation. During the preparation of Sn-Pb perovskites, ABH suppresses interfacial oxidation by reducing Sn4+ defects and converts to p-aminobenzaldehyde (ABD), which suppresses photogenerated hole-induced Sn2+ oxidation, aligning energy levels for efficient hole extraction. The in situ redox-converted molecule stabilizes the buried interface during both device fabrication and operation, reduces non-radiative recombination and enhances stability. The resulting narrow-bandgap Sn-Pb PSC achieves a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 25.4% (certified 25.2%) with an open-circuit voltage of 0.92 V and a fill factor of 83.4%. Integrated into monolithic all-perovskite TSCs, the device delivers a PCE of 31.1% (certified 30.8%) together with enhanced thermal (ISOS-D-2I, 85 °C) and operational stability (ISOS-L-1I) under inert conditions.

#688. What will returning Magill bring to Northern Ireland?

Simone Magill made her return to football as a late substitute for Birmingham City against Manchester United on Sunday

After 13 months away, Simone Magill made her return to football as a late substitute in Birmingham City's WSL defeat by Manchester United on Sunday.

It was a moment that had been a long time coming for the 31-year-old, who gave birth to her daughter, Skye, in May and has been building towards stepping back on the pitch.

Now, she will hope to make her international return with Northern Ireland in a friendly against Greece on Friday.

"It's been some time since I've been here in a playing capacity, so it's really nice just to be back in the mix again," NI captain Magill told BBC Sport NI.

"I officially made my comeback at the weekend and it was really nice to have done that. I'm really looking forward to doing that here at home in front of the fans and my family as well."

'You can be a mum and a footballer - they can co-exist'

Greece friendlies an opportunity to build - Andrews

In an interview with BBC Sport in October, Magill spoke about how being both a mum and a footballer can "co-exist".

While she was not ready to play any role in the matches, Magill, Skye and her husband Mark were all in camp for the World Cup play-off with Portugal last month, all with an eye of integrating into international duty as a family.

Having played just a handful of minutes, Northern Ireland manager Michael McArdle said that while he was "delighted" to have Magill back, how much she plays across the double-header would be in collaboration with Birmingham and his captain.

"With the circumstances around this one, I'm very mindful that I need to build accordingly and I really need to listen to myself as well," Magill added.

"To even be back in this capacity this soon after giving birth, for me, is just unbelievable.

"I have no major expectations. I'm just really happy to be here and be a part of it, and if I do come on, that'll be even better."

Watch live on BBC iPlayer and the BBC Sport app and website

Friday's match against Greece will be Northern Ireland's first friendly in three years.

The sides will then play again on Tuesday at 16:00 GMT, and both matches can be streamed live on BBC iPlayer and the BBC Sport app and website.

The matches will act as preparation for the Nations League campaign in February, when Northern Ireland face tricky tests in the form of Poland, Finland and Belarus.

McArdle is developing a young squad and Magill says she hopes to bring "leadership and experience to really help us all move forward".

"We've obviously had a transition in the last year whilst I've been out, it's been nice to come back in and just feel where we're at, get on the grass with the girls and see, 'how can I help, what can I bring?'," she added.

"I'm very much looking forward to just getting back in the mix and helping try to bring the young players forward, use that experience and let's hold on to the ball, let's get into the final third, let's have a go, be brave - all of the attributes that we're known for.

"We're an underdog nation, so it's getting that across to the younger members in the squad to say, 'let's have a go with these teams and not be afraid'."

Simone Magill (centre) is set to make her Northern Ireland return against Greece

In her absence over the past year, Northern Ireland have used a number of different options in the centre forward role.

Winger Lauren Wade has shown her versatility by playing centrally, while Kess Elmore and Cora Chambers have also played up top.

Along with Magill, Portsmouth striker Kerry Beattie is also back in the squad to bolster McArdle's striking options.

"We've loads of young ones snapping at my heels. It's great, that's what we want.

"I feel we're more competitive now than ever. You never know who's going to be coming into the squad. Certainly, in more recent years, you kind of knew the squad every single time, whereas that's not the case now.

"We've got some exciting youth coming through, so it's their time now to shine."

Magill added that Northern Ireland are "heading in a new direction" ahead of the Nations League campaign next year, and the friendlies with Greece give an opportunity for the team to grow in a pressure-free environment.

"We're coming into a brand new campaign and it's really nice that we have a friendly window just now.

"We haven't had one in a very, very long time, so this is a brilliant opportunity to get us all back together, get the new faces in, get some more experience, learn things, try things.

"I'm really excited about where we're going."

#687. German firms eye Africa as global trade shocks hit traditional markets

German businesses are optimistic about Africa, but Berlin's cautious approach to risk is holding them back from cashing in on the opportunities that their competitors from countries like the UAE and Turkey are seizing.

"Africa is a land of opportunity." "The German-African relationship is a win-win." "The continent is the market of the future."

That's what many business leaders and politicians have to say about Africa at the sixth edition of the German-African Business Summit in Accra, Ghana. While these descriptions aren't new, there's a palpable sense of urgency and seriousness this time.

German firms are increasingly viewing Africa as an attractive destination as they scramble to find new markets amid wars in Ukraine and Iran, high energy prices, punishing US tariffs and slowing growth in traditional markets like China.

"For a long time, many German companies had a secure source of revenue from the major export markets in North America and China, but the geopolitical ruptures of our time have undermined this certainty," German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier said during the event.

"One could also say that it is time for new horizons, time to take a closer look at economic opportunities still waiting for us."

Africa is home to some of the fastest growing economies in the world, like Ethiopia and Rwanda. Even as European and other advanced economies contend with declining working-age populations, Africa is expected to add hundreds of millions of workers in the next few decades, emerging as a key source of future labor.

Germany has already signed a migration pact with Kenya and is working on one with Ghana as it seeks to attract skilled workers to help ease acute labor shortages in certain sectors at home.

Even as Africa remains one of the poorest regions in the world, economic growth in parts of the continent has created a larger and more affluent consumer class over the past three decades. This group is aspirational and a growing source of demand for many of the goods that German firms want to sell, from cars to cosmetics.

The continent, with its mineral wealth and renewable energy potential, is central to European Union efforts to diversify its sources of critical raw materials and reduce reliance on China-dominated supply chains.

It is also playing an increasingly important role in strengthening the EU's energy security after the bloc phased out most energy imports from Russia.

German firms have committed to invest billions of euros in green hydrogen projects in countries such as Mauritania and Namibia.

"We don't have the capital to develop them [natural resources]. So foreign investors are coming to help us develop those resources. Whilst we are getting jobs and industrialization is taking place, they are also making profits," said Amin Amidu Sulemani, energy and infrastructure commissioner at the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS).

"It's not a relationship where we send raw materials outside of Africa every time, when we can actually process them here," he told DW.

Despite Africa's growing economic appeal, many obstacles to investment remain, including corruption and governance concerns, unreliable energy supplies, foreign exchange risk and poor infrastructure.

African leaders say they are working to address these challenges and improve the ease of doing business.

Yet while German companies have largely remained on the sidelines, competitors from countries such as the UAE, Turkey and India have made significant inroads across the continent.

German firms enjoy a strong reputation in Africa because of their engineering expertise, vocational training programs and long-term industrial investments, which are more likely to create stable jobs than investments in extractive industries.

However, they have struggled to translate that goodwill into a larger commercial presence. Africa, for instance, accounts for less than 2% of the total foreign investment made by German firms over the past several decades.

Business leaders complain that German firms lack adequate financing and risk protection for projects in Africa. They also criticize excessive bureaucracy and the absence of a coherent German strategy, with engagement fragmented across ministries and agencies.

Industry bodies say German institutions and firms often perceive risks too broadly, treating diverse African markets as if they pose the same level of risk.

"German companies can be a bit more bold and maybe also innovative in the way they approach the continent," Khadi Camara, deputy CEO of the German-African Business Association, told DW. "We see that in the companies that are successful, they don't do business as usual. Every country has its nuances that companies keep in mind and say, okay, this model works here, that model works there."

The 2026 World Investment Report by UN trade body UNCTAD showed that investors from the Gulf and Asia are becoming important sources of investment in Africa, especially in energy, logistics, real estate and infrastructure.

The UAE has been a major investor in greenfield megaprojects in recent years, including the $34 billion (€31 billion) Infinity Power renewable energy project in Mauritania, the $24 billion Ras El Hikma real estate development project in Egypt and the $6 billion H2 Global Energy hydrogen project in Tunisia.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Business leaders are calling for better financing and guarantees, and more risk-sharing and fewer bureaucratic hurdles.

Meanwhile, others, including the German president, are urging German businesses to take on more risk and seize opportunities in Africa. Otherwise, they risk being edged out by foreign rivals.

"Be curious, take risks and invest in our common future," Steinmeier said.

#686. Why KMI Panel frustrates referees too - and impacts their salary

Referees rely on the opinions of former players to determine a significant part of their annual salary

It has become something of a Wednesday morning ritual for fans. At 10am, the Premier League releases the latest votes of its Key Match Incidents Panel.

For four seasons, the KMI Panel was a clandestine operation. It was distributed to clubs only, but it would still find its way out into the public domain.

This season, it began being released to the public.

Yet little is really understood about the KMI Panel.

Why does it exist? Is it just protecting referees? And does it really mean anything?

For referees, the last question is more important than you might realise.

The votes, which ultimately say whether referees have got a decision right or wrong, create a merit table of performance - and this impacts their salary.

"It depends where you are on the list," former Premier League referee Graham Scott said. "But if you're in the middle, then it might be 25% of your take-home. So it's substantial."

For the officials, these are not decisions being taken by their bosses.

Their performance reviews are effectively outsourced to a group of former players.

The results can be inconsistent and frustrating as much for the referees as they are for the fans.

Let's take a look at how a referee's salary works in the Premier League.

A Premier League official will earn, on average, about Â£175,000 per year. The scale will run between Â£125,000 and Â£250,000.

Think that is unduly high? Referees in Spain's La Liga are the highest paid in the world, according to Marca, with an average yearly salary of Â£221,000.

Premier League officials are about on par with those in the German Bundesliga and Italian Serie A.

In England, there is a guaranteed base wage of 50%. This will differ depending on the seniority and experience of an official.

Michael Oliver would be at the top of the bracket, a newcomer like Farai Hallam at the other end.

The other 50% is based upon a set of variables, with match fees a major part.

Each on-field appointment is worth a little over Â£1000, with a VAR game slightly less.

Last season, Anthony Taylor refereed the most Premier League games, 31, followed by Chris Kavanagh, 30, and Michael Oliver, 29.

Kavanagh and Oliver worked as VAR on a handful of occasions, while Taylor did not do any.

Stuart Attwell had the most combined appointments at 52, with 25 games as a referee and 27 as a VAR.

Finally, there is the subjective element - the KMI Panel.

The votes determine the annual bonus payments for all officials.

Until 2022, referees' body Pro Ref, or PGMOL as it was known until this summer, used to do its own assessment of its referees' decisions.

But clubs grew restless, feeling referees were marking their own homework.

It is made up of five members. Three are former players and coaches, plus there is a representative for the Premier League and one for Pro Ref.

Their identities remain secret, with the former professionals selected from a pool on rotation.

What you won't see on the published version is that each incident is given a difficulty rating, ranging from one to five, which is taken into account when drawing up the referees' merit table.

All this really is, of course, is another layer of subjectivity. On top of the referees, VAR, players and coaches.

"People complain about the consistency of referees on field, of VAR interventions, or otherwise," said Scott, who now acts as the refereeing expert for the Athletic.

"But then, if you look at the KMI Panel outcomes, they're also inconsistent."

It is a view shared by Andy Davies, who retired as a Championship referee last year.

"Naturally, there will always be a level of interest given as it provides a significant part of income for the season," Davies said.

"But ultimately, the KMI Panel lacks any real credibility amongst referees."

Graham Scott was a Premier League referee for 10 years and acted as a VAR for more than 100 matches

Referees are scored on their on-field decision-making. If an error has been corrected by the VAR, it still counts as a mistake for the merit table.

Those at the top of the table will be rewarded well, while those at the bottom are not likely to receive much of a bonus payment at all.

Let's take a look at the numbers from last season.

Michael Oliver was the top referee, getting 93.5% of KMIs correct. John Brooks, Darren England and Simon Hooper were very marginally behind.

For other referees, the borderline decisions, ones which are the most subjective and sit in the grey areas, can be an issue.

One vote could be the difference between a referee being right or wrong. And a place on the merit table, impacting how much they get paid.

Last season, Sam Barrott and Jarred Gillett were both told they made four errors to a 2:3 vote.

Attwell, meanwhile, had three of the more high-profile incidents go in his favour to a 3:2 vote.

"The ones that sit in the margins can be very contentious and inconsistent," said Scott.

"You think, well, how can that be right? You know, that's not definitive, is it? It could have gone either way.

"But there seems to be a reluctance to allow that 'seen them given' sort of mentality, neither right nor wrong.

"Relying on such a small group of people to be so definitive, especially when they vote 3:2, is unhealthy and unhelpful."

As well as determining the merit table for each referee's salary, what the KMI Panel says can guide how games are refereed.

The members of the KMI Panel can be influenced by public opinion, and inconsistency means referees are often having to change the way they approach games, only to be told it is wrong.

"I have spoken to many referees, even this season," Davies said. "And they have no idea which way the panel is going to fall at times, or which way Pro Ref are going to vote because of how political it can be."

Scott used the example of holding when an attacker is offside.

In December last year, Brentford's Dango Ouattara was pulled back against Leeds. The penalty was cancelled by the VAR for offside. The KMI Panel voted 5:0 it was correct.

Last month, Arsenal were not given a penalty against Hull, when an offside Kai Havertz was pulled back by Nobel Mendy. The KMI Panel voted 5:0 it was incorrect.

"One minute we're told football expects an offside," Scott said. "Okay, we'll deliver that for you. We do it again, and they say the opposite.

"Referees get confused on the back of that mixed feedback. It just shows how the system's flawed.

"The game can afford to invest more in this process, and a properly independent approach."

For now, at least, referees have no choice but to rely on the KMI Panel to determine a chunk of their salary.

#683. Gisele Bündchen Shares Rare Family Photos in Honor of Thanksgiving

Gisele Bündchen shared a glimpse inside her life as a mom of three in honor of Thanksgiving: “Gratitude is contagious.”

Gisele Bündchen is giving a peek inside her private world.

The supermodel—who shares kids Benjamin, 16, and Vivian, 13, with ex-husband Tom Brady as well as a 21-month-old son with husband Joaquim Valente—shared never-before-seen family photos in honor of Thanksgiving.

“The amount of goodness we experience in life depends on our ability to notice it,” Gisele captioned her Nov. 26 Instagram post alongside a slew of family memories. “Gratitude is contagious, and the more we can appreciate the beauty around us, the more joy we bring into our lives and the lives of others.”

"May we always find something to be grateful for, not just today, but every day," she added. "Happy Thanksgiving! Sending you all so much love."

Offering a closer look into her model life, the 46-year-old shared a photo holding her youngest child up over her head as they enjoyed a day at the beach.

Meanwhile, another snap showed the toddler getting some father-son time as Joaquim held his hand by the ocean at sunset. And later in the photo dump, the trio all posed together as Gisele planted a kiss on the jiu-jitsu instructor’s cheek.

Allowing her fans to strut even further into her life away from the runway, Gisele also shared insight into her blended family’s sweet bond, with one photo capturing her eldest two kids sitting outside while their little brother clung on tight to Vivian.

The teen also cuddled up to her baby bro as they traveled on an airplane. While Vivian—donning a bright pink top—placed a kiss on the baby’s head, he cozied in close for an extra dose of sibling love.

And Benjamin definitely wasn’t left out on the sidelines as another photo captured the shirtless teen holding his brother on his hip as they admired LED lights.

Elsewhere in the post, Gisele also shed light on her wellness routine, which included practicing yoga, eating açaí bowls and bonding with animals.

And while the Lessons author—who tied the knot with Joaquim in December 2025—is notoriously private about her personal life, this Turkey Day wouldn’t be the first time she gave thanks to her husband.

After all, she gave her him some love on his 39th birthday, calling him a “great man” on his special day.

“How lucky I am,” she continued on Instagram Stories Nov. 7 in a message translated from Portuguese. “I love you so much!”

As for what makes him a model life partner? She previously thanked him for “leading by example, and for the values you embody, love, humility, integrity, discipline, kindness and consistency.”

“You are an incredible role model,” she added in the June 21 Instagram post. “We are all so grateful for you, and we love you so much.”

The “Honey Bee” singer and “Hollaback Girl” hitmaker snuggled in close as they expressed gratitude for their fans. As Shelton wrote on Instagram Nov. 26, “Hoping everybody has a happy Thanksgiving!!! Thankful for y'all!!!!”

The supermodel and jiu jitsu instructor showed off their model life with their 21-month-old son.

“The amount of goodness we experience in life depends on our ability to notice it," Bündchen captioned her Nov. 26 Instagram post, which also featured pictures of her and ex-husband Tom Brady's kids Benjamin, 16, and Vivian, 13. "Gratitude is contagious, and the more we can appreciate the beauty around us, the more joy we bring into our lives and the lives of others."

She added, "May we always find something to be grateful for, not just today, but every day. Happy Thanksgiving! Sending you all so much love."

It was a celebration for the girls as Dunham marked her first Thanksgiving as a mom alongside husband Luis Felber.

As she captioned the Nov. 26 Instagram post as the family went on a stroll, "Thankful."

You oughta know how excited the country music star is about the holiday season.

“Time for a little more peace, love and cowboys,” she wrote on Instagram Nov. 26. “Let the holiday shenanigans begin happy Thanksgiving from my family to y’all’s!”

The Freaky Friday star got reflective this Thanksgiving as she shared an image of herself stretching while enjoying an ocean view.

"Going to turn off the noise for a moment," she wrote on Instagram Nov. 26. "To all out there in this vast environment that we opt into, that if you're lucky enough to have one, the Thanksgiving meal is not hard. It's a roasted bird and potatoes."

"What's hard are the people with their binary and rigid ideas and judgments and petty selfishness," she added. "Today let's all be like Dolly [Parton] and be welcoming and gentle and generous."

The Red Table Talk host showed off her family's extravagant Thanksgiving set-up.

"Preparing for Thanksgiving dinner at the family abode," she wrote on Instagram Nov. 26. "Happy Day of thanks to you all and may you, your families and loved ones continue to be lifted and showered by the gifts of grace from the Highest. They may not always show up how we want them to … but they are there."

#681. Duran scores late Celtic winner to keep Europa League hopes alive

Torreense vs Celtic. UEFA Europa League Round 1.

Campo Manuel MarquesAttendance: Attendance4,971.

Report from the Europa League clash between Torreense and Celtic at Campo Manuel Marques; Javi Vazquez' own-goal put Celtic in front; Dany Jean levelled before the break; substitute Camilo Duran headed in a late winner for the Hoops; Martin O'Neill's side are up to 25th

Football Journalist @AlisonGConroy

Camilo Duran came off the bench to keep Celtic's Europa League hopes alive with a vital win against Torreense.

The Colombian striker peeled away to the back post to meet a cross from fellow substitute James Forrest, guiding a downward header into the net in the 85th minute.

Duran's 15th goal of the season secured a 2-1 victory over the Portuguese second-tier side and moved Celtic on to six points in the Europa League. His latest decisive contribution follows a match-winning double off the bench in the Hoops' comeback victory over Besiktas last time out.

Celtic took the lead in the ninth minute when Javi Vazquez turned Jota's cross into his own net, with Hyun-jun Yang lurking behind him.

However, the Portuguese Cup winners hit back 10 minutes later after some hesitant defending from the visitors. Alex Alfaro rattled the crossbar with a 22-yard effort, but neither Kieran Tierney nor Colby Donovan could deal with the resulting loose balls, allowing Haiti international Dany Jean to volley home the equaliser.

Celtic dominated possession after the break but struggled to create clear-cut opportunities until Duran's late intervention secured all three points.

The Hoops' attention now turns to Hearts on Sunday, live on Sky Sports, as they look to remain top of the Scottish Premiership.

Their next Europa League match is away to Omonia Nicosia on December 10.

2: CLOSE! Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain sends in a corner, it's flicked on by Liam Scales but Hyun-jun Yang can't knock the ball in before it's cleared.

9: GOAL CELTIC! Javi Vazquez tries to clear Jota's cross but turns it into his own net.

19: GOAL TORREENSE! Alex Alfaro's effort rattles the underside of the bar, Celtic fail to make a clearance and Dany Jean fires in the equaliser.

33: SAVE! Jota's powerful strike is pushed over the bar by Adriel.

36: OFF THE LINE! More awful defending from Celtic, but Liam Scales manages to head the ball clear.

47: SAVE! Jota tries to chip the ball over the goalkeeper but he manages to pluck the ball out of the air.

53: BLOCK! Jota is continuing to cause problems for the hosts as he sends in a cross for Kieran Tierney, which is headed behind.

61: CLOSE! Jean looks to squeeze in a shot at the near post, but it's just wide.

69: CHANCE! A misplaced pass from Oliver Sorensen lets Musa Drammeh get a shot away. Thankfully for Celtic it's wide.

70: LET OFF FOR CELTIC! Trouble at the back again gives Drammeh space to get a shot away, but the former Hearts striker is inches wide.

84: GOAL CELTIC! Camilo Duran rises at the back post to head in James Forrest's cross. Celtic are back ahead.

Jota looked back to his best despite not scoring or providing an assist.

In his first European appearance for Celtic since 2025, the winger was a pest for the Portuguese side until he was replaced by James Forrest.

He created chances with some brilliant crossing with one turned in by Vazquez for the opening goal.

He has been sensational since arriving in the summer and he saved Celtic again.

But it was far from a perfect performance in Portugal.

Once again, slack defending and individual errors proved costly, allowing Torreense to remain well in the game.

Record signing Kasper Hogh started, but once again did not score. He is lacking in confidence, but how long do you stick with a striker who is not putting the ball in the net?

Celtic manager Martin O'Neill on TNT Sports:

"I'm just delighted to have won, it keeps us going if nothing else. We've got six points on the board and we've still a couple of games to go.

"From an almost impossible position, having lost the first three games, we've given ourselves some hope.

"Three points tonight were of vital importance. There's lots we can still do to improve our game."

Asked about Camilo Duran, he added: "He's just a magnificent footballer.

"15 goals and we're not into December, he's been flying. He's a terrific player, and that's two games he's come up big for us."

Celtic winger Jota speaking to TNT Sports after his first European appearance for almost two years:

"It was a long road and I did my maximum to be as fit as possible.

"Right now, it's all about enjoying life. No expectations, just be professional and having the responsibility of being a Celtic player.

"It wasn't easy. I think we just had to stick with our plan and in the end it worked out, that's the most important thing.

"We must believe [Celtic can qualify]. Every game is a different battle, we know what to do."
